title: A formula with a shared number switches between recognized and not recognized as the slider moves, so the deformation, program, lamps and note flicker
detail: The 7-point probe guard in recChain (funcs.js) decides recognition at the current value of a, so the reading of a high-degree rational changes from one slider step to the next. DESIGN says a shared number never decides the structure, but here it does. The cause is that the expanded-coefficient 'rational' step misses the 1e-9 tolerance at one probe for some values of a and passes at others. Each switch changes the natural path (the deformation at t = 0.5 jumps between the 'rational' catalog path and the formula's own path), the GPU program key, the Inspector note ('Recognized as Rational ...' appears and disappears) and the build cost. Before this change, the formula kept one path for the whole drag.
evidence: Node, a stepped by 0.01 as the slider does (R = recognized, . = not). \frac{(z+a)^{12}}{(z-a)^{12}} on a ∈ [0.5, 0.9]: RRRRRRR.R...R............................ (9 of 41). \frac{(z+a)^{8}}{(z-a)^{8}}: RRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR.RR...R....R....R (29 of 41). Headless Chrome at 1440x900, a = 0.7 ± 0.2 over 1.6 s, before → after. Plain drag: frames p95 16.8 → 18.7 ms, max 24.8 → 38.8 ms. Drag with the deformation open at t = 0.5: p95 16.8 → 18.4 ms, max 18.0 → 46.2 ms. The note was seen both empty and as 'Recognized as Rational: uses the natural paths…' within one drag. Files: raw/review-perf/c1.js, c1.out (A_rat12a vs B_rat12a).
fix: Make the decision independent of the values of shared numbers. Either decide once from the structure, with the probes evaluated at fixed values of the shared numbers and the result cached per (parameter-free tree key, cut), or refuse a generic 'rational' or 'poly' reading of degree above about 4 when the formula contains a shared number. A product of powers of linear factors fits the 'zp' step (zeros and poles in product form, already on the GPU), which is exact and needs no probe tolerance (see frperf-3).

title: Dragging through a special value changes the chain's shape mid-drag: an 80 ms GPU recompile, a pending right pane and a jump in the deformation
detail: The reading depends on which coefficients are exactly 0 or 1 at the current value. In z^{2}+az the step is Polynomial for a ≠ 0 and Integer power at a = 0.00, a value the 0.01 slider lands on. In \frac{z^2-a}{z+1} the step is Affine → Joukowski → Affine, then → Translate at a = 0.75 (the scale becomes exactly 1), then not recognized at a = 1 (the removable point). Every change of shape is a new program signature, so the shader compiles in the middle of the drag. The inverse path goes 'pending' for a frame, and the deformation's natural path jumps. Without recognition, z^{2}+az kept one program and one path for the whole drag. The note also flips between 'Integer power' and 'Polynomial'.
evidence: Headless Chrome at 1440x900, slider values rounded to 0.01, before → after. z^{2}+az, a = 0 ± 0.3: max frame 17.7 → 83.1 ms (one 82 ms long task), with the deformation open 43.2 → 63.0 ms. The paths seen were inverse → pending → inverse. \frac{z^2-a}{z+1}, a = 1 ± 0.3: max 52.7 → 74.6 ms, with the deformation open 17.1 → 66.9 ms. Five distinct path and note states were seen in one drag. Node, a stepped by 0.01: z^{2}+az gives poly ×60 and pown ×1; \frac{z^2-a}{z+1} gives affine>joukowski>affine ×59, affine>joukowski>add ×1 and not recognized ×1. Files: raw/review-perf/c1.out (A_z2az, A_jka vs B_*).
fix: Keep the step's shape while a shared number moves. When a coefficient that holds a shared number becomes 0 or 1, keep the general step: poly with a zero coefficient, affine with scale 1, and the same Joukowski chain. Name the steps from the structure, not from the values. Where the value really changes the map (a removable point at a = 1), keep the last chain's program and let only the inverse/forward choice change. A test in t_recognize could step each corpus formula with a over its slider grid and require one program key.

title: A recognized product of powers is evaluated from expanded coefficients: much less accurate near repeated zeros, in float32 on the GPU
detail: multi() sends every rational node through Inverse.rationalForm, and ratChain makes a 'poly' or 'rational' step from the expanded coefficients. The step's f (r.f = rec.f on the CPU) and its GPU plan (Horner on uniform coefficients, glsl.js case 'poly'/'rational') then replace the formula as written. Before, the formula was evaluated as typed, with factored powers through genCustom. Near a cluster of zeros, Horner on the expanded coefficients cancels catastrophically. In float32 the phase of f is wrong in a visible disk. The 7 probes pass because they lie away from the clusters. Not checked in a rendered picture (time box). The numbers below emulate the GPU's float32 Horner exactly.
evidence: (z-1)^5(z+1)^5 is read as Polynomial, degree 10, co = [1,0,-5,0,10,0,-10,0,5,0,-1]. Float32 Horner (Math.fround at every operation) against the formula at z = 1 + r·e^{0.7i}: relative error 2e-3 at r = 0.1, 3e-2 at r = 0.05, 1.3 at r = 0.02 (phase error 0.22 rad). The CPU (float64) step's relative error is 1.3e-8 at r = 0.02, against about 1e-16 for the formula. Above degree 12 the probes already catch it: \frac{(z+1)^{20}}{(z-1)^{20}} fails at the probe 0.9+0.05i with relative error 0.99999. Script: raw/review-perf/why.js and the inline check in this review.
fix: Read a product or quotient of powers of affine factors as the 'zp' catalog step (a ∏(z−ζ)/(z−p), product form on the CPU and GPU). Its inverse renderer is the same rational inverse. Keep the expanded 'poly'/'rational' reading only when the formula was typed expanded, or when the degree is ≤ 4 and the roots are simple. Also add probes near the formula's own zeros and poles to the guard.

title: Failed recognition attempts cost a full extra build on every keystroke and every slider frame
detail: recChain runs inside the custom build, and app.js rebuild() builds every step on each keystroke and each slider frame. The plane menu (app.js:8801) also builds the typed formula on every keystroke. For a rational formula the reader computes the exact normal form, builds every catalog step with its natural-path data (ratPath for a 'rational'), then runs the probes. When the probes refuse the reading, all of that is discarded and the formula's own customNat is built as before. Formulas that end up unrecognized therefore pay the most. Nothing is cached between rebuilds.
evidence: Node (JIT warm, 20 builds averaged), Funcs.build('custom') before → after. \frac{(z+1)^{20}}{(z-1)^{20}}: 3.3 → 13.0 ms (rationalForm 3.0 ms plus the 'rational' buildVals 6.1 ms, then refused). \frac{(z+a)^{12}}{(z-a)^{12}}: 1.0 → 5.5 ms. \frac{(az+b)^{8}}{(cz+d)^{8}}: 0.6 → 2.4 ms. \frac{(z^2+1)^{6}(z-2)^{5}}{(z+3)^{7}(z^2-z+1)^{4}}: 2.5 → 6.7 ms. All 163 corpus formulas plus 21 extra: 21.9 → 40.2 ms in total. Browser: Params.set('a') p50 2.5 → 5.6 ms for (z+a)^12/(z-a)^12. Typing \frac{(z+1)^{20}}{(z-1)^{20}} one character at a time: the slowest input handler went from 5.8 to 17.6 ms, over a frame budget. Small formulas are unaffected (z^{i}: input p50 1.5 → 1.2 ms). Files: raw/review-perf/before.json, after.json, bench_build.js, c1.out.
fix: Cache the reading by (tree key with shared numbers by name, cut) and re-evaluate only the values on a slider frame. Run the probes on the reading's coefficients (CX.polyEval) before building any catalog step. Build the catalog steps' natural-path data lazily, or only after the probes pass. Skip the reader in the plane menu's preview build (it reads only props and error).

title: The Inspector note is not quiet: it is on every recognized formula, uses internal jargon, and names a parameter the user never typed
detail: b.recNote is appended to the branch note on every recognized step, even the trivial ones (z^2 + az: 'Recognized as Polynomial: uses the exact fast renderer'). 'Exact fast renderer' / 'точная быстрая отрисовка' is an internal term that appears nowhere else in the UI. The catalog labels leak their parameter letters: \frac{1}{2i}\log\frac{1+iz}{1-iz} is 'Möbius → Logarithm → Multiply by c', but the user typed no c. In Russian at 1440 px the line takes 4 lines in the 262 px Inspector column. While a shared number is dragged, the note changes text or disappears (frperf-1, frperf-2). For z^{i} the line now reads '… Drag the seam in the input plane. cut 180°. Recognized as …', four sentences where there was one. It matches the catalog step, but it is long. Not checked at 390 px: the Inspector is closed by default on the phone (.inote has a zero-size box).
evidence: Headless Chrome, \frac{1}{2i}\log\frac{1+iz}{1-iz}: EN 'log, √ and powers use arg ∈ (−180°, 180°]. Recognized as Möbius → Logarithm → Multiply by c: uses the exact fast renderer.' RU '… Распознано как Дробно-линейная → Логарифм → Умножение на c: используется точная быстрая отрисовка.' Screenshots: raw/review-perf/note_1440_en.png and note_1440_ru.png. Drag states in c1.out (A_z2az, A_rat12a, A_jka).
fix: Show it only when recognition changes something the user sees (the path, the cut, the lamps), as one short clause: 'Same as Möbius → Logarithm → Scale.' / 'Как цепочка: Дробно-линейная → Логарифм → Растяжение.' Drop 'exact fast renderer', or move it to the title tooltip. Use labels without parameter letters (Scale, Translate). Keep the text stable while a slider moves.

title: A formula read as n steps plays them in one step's time: each part is n times faster than the same catalog chain
detail: asChain and recPlan put step j on [j/n, (j+1)/n] inside one app step, while the catalog chain gives each step a full unit. A typed e^{2z} now plays Scale and then Exp in half the time each, and \sin z+\cos z plays three parts in thirds. That differs from the catalog chain the note names, and from before (one smooth generic zoom over the whole interval). It is not a frame-rate problem: the deformation holds 60 fps. It is a feel and speed difference that the user may notice when comparing a typed formula with its catalog chain. AS-BUILT lists it as an open point.
evidence: funcs.js asChain r.hom (s = t·n, j = floor(s)); glsl.js recPlan h (float s = t * n.0). raw/browser_after.json: all deformations at 60 fps.
fix: Either give the sub-steps time in proportion to the catalog chain (show the step count in the morph timeline and stretch the step's duration to n units), or say in the deformation caption that the steps share one step's time. A product decision for the user.

title: What holds: the user's z^{complex} case, Möbius drags, typing small formulas and unrecognized formulas without numbers
detail: z^{i} and z^i are both inverse-rendered as the catalog Complex power. Typing z^{i} costs the same as before: input handler p50 1.5 → 1.2 ms, two-frame latency p50 31.9 → 32.3 ms. Dragging a in \frac{az+1}{z+a} holds 60 fps, max 17.6 ms (17.9 with the deformation open). The GPU program build (GLChain.build) is no slower for any corpus formula (≤ 0.12 ms). astSig keeps shared numbers as names, so an unrecognized formula still does not recompile on a slider frame. Not measured here: pan and zoom at 390 px, and export. The builder's raw/browser_after.json covers pan, drag and deformation at 1440. Export uses the same built chain, so the frperf-1/2 flicker would also change a recorded parameter sweep.
